newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro/US stocks and dollar slip, gold weak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro/US stocks and dollar slip, gold weak.

text.p: Key European stock markets, having followed Wall Street's overnight cue to scale new peaks on Wednesday morning, ran out of steam in the afternoon as shares dropped in New York and concern over interest rates returned.
Gold, in contrast, hit 3-1/4 year lows below $352 after investment funds took flight but then revived to top $354 and trim its losses amid buying on New York's Comex futures market.
"It might have a bit of upside potential this afternoon but the weakness is not over yet," one bullion dealer cautioned.

The gold market, depressed by competition from a firm dollar and booming shares, has taken an extra blow from news that the Dutch central bank sold 300 tonnes of the metal -- prompting fears that other banks could follow suit.

On the currency market, the dollar flirted with a 30-month high against the German currency of 1.60 marks and a 46-month peak of 117.48 yen before slipping back. But dealers said market sentiment for the U.S. currency was still positive.
"I wouldn't be surprised if we have a bit of a correction but overall I don't think there's any major change in the attitude towards the dollar," said Peter Wood, dealer at Bank of Boston in London.
Hoping that a dose of higher interest rates would not be needed yet, London, Frankfurt, Paris and several other bourses moved up smartly into uncharted territory in the morning.
The London stock market, where the value of blue chips in the FTSE 100 index had added 111 points or about 18.8 billion pounds ($31.4 billion) in the week's two previous sessions, rose at the start.

But unexpectedly strong British economic data, showing a 45,100 drop in the December jobless total to a six-year low of 1.88 million, soon spoiled the mood and roused the spectre of higher rates, sending Europe's busiest stock market lower.
"There certainly are more people looking for a rate hike today than there were yesterday," said one London dealer.
Other bourses were also unsettled when Wall Street took profits from its recent winning streak.
"I think this sell-off is a bit overdue," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co in New York.

The Dow Jones industrial average, having risen 53.11 to a record 6,762.29 on Tuesday, was down around 40 points by the end of the New York morning after losing more than 50 points at one stage in line with weakness in bonds.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke met Eddie George, the Governor of the Bank of England, on Wednesday afternoon to discuss British monetary policy. British interest rates are expected to rise before an election, which must be held by mid-May, but had not generally been tipped to go up just yet.
However, some analysts said a rate rise could not be ruled out after the jobs data. Thursday morning's money market operation would normally be the time when any rate change would be signalled.

In Frankfurt, Germany's DAX index of leading shares at first neared the elusive 3,000-point level and finally registered a record close in floor trading, up 1.3 percent on the day, despite slipping from all-time trading peaks hit in the morning.
Shares were boosted by a general market boom, benign U.S. consumer price data and the dollar's rally, which made stars of chemical shares and other dollar-sensitive stocks.
"A dollar at this level is going to mean windfall profits for a lot of companies and we will see that reflected in earnings statements at the year end," said one Frankfurt dealer.

Paris stocks also pushed to new highs before slipping into the minus column. Traders said a consolidation was natural after recent gains and with background concerns such as health worries over Russian President Boris Yeltsin and lower U.S. bond prices.
Following Tuesday's all-time highs by a dozen bourses, Amsterdam, Athens, Brussels, Copenhagen, Lisbon, Istanbul, Oslo Stockholm and Zurich were at or near new peaks on Wednesday.
In Asian trading, Hong Kong stocks also surged to record highs but Japanese markets, which have provided plenty of interest for those elsewhere recently, were on holiday.
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was quoted around 117.10 yen and 1.5895 marks, compared with 116.92 and 1.5957 late in Europe on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 9.3 points lower at 4,158.9 after an earlier record high of 4,191.5.
Frankfurt's 30-share DAX ended floor trade at a record close of 2,988.45, up 39.57, after a new intraday peak of 2,997.05. In later computerised trade, the IBIS DAX slipped back to 2,976.56.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 14.16 at 2,387.98 after scoring a record 2,418.93 in the morning.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $354.45 in the afternoon and ended London business around $354.15. Its low was $351.80, compared with the previous close of $357.55. Silver was down one cent at $4.70.
